Design a geometric model consisting of two square plates, each with an edge length of 140mm and a thickness of 10mm. Position these plates so that they intersect at a 90-degree angle, creating an L-shape configuration. On one of these plates, incorporate a square cutout measuring 45x45mm. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step plan (no execution yet)

1. Establish a right-hand Cartesian coordinate system with the origin at the lower-left, top-surface corner of the first (horizontal) plate.  
   • X-axis points along the long edge of the plate.  
   • Y-axis runs along the second in-plane edge.  
   • Z-axis points upward (thickness direction).

2. Create the HORIZONTAL plate (Plate A).  
   • Geometry: 140 mm (X) × 140 mm (Y) × 10 mm (Z).  
   • Block base-point: (0 , 0 , 0).  
   • This is the very first solid, so subtraction = False.

3. Create the VERTICAL plate (Plate B) that stands upright and intersects Plate A at 90°.  
   • Give it the same face size but rotate it so its thickness (10 mm) runs along X and its tall sides run along Y and Z.  
   • Geometry: 10 mm (X) × 140 mm (Y) × 140 mm (Z).  
   • To seat it centrally in Plate A, shift it 65 mm in X ( (140-10)/2 ) so the 10 mm-thick web straddles the mid-line of Plate A.  
   • Base-point: (65 , 0 , 0).  
   • subtraction = False (it adds material).

4. Add the square through-cut in Plate A.  
   • Size: 45 mm × 45 mm × 10 mm (full thickness of Plate A).  
   • Centre it on Plate A: the lower-left corner of the cutout is at ((140-45)/2 = 47.5 , same for Y).  
   • Block base-point: (47.5 , 47.5 , 0).  
   • subtraction = True (this removes material).

5. Sequence the three block calls in one single block() function call by giving arrays for every parameter:  
   • x_size  = [140, 10, 45]  
   • y_size  = [140, 140, 45]  
   • z_size  = [10, 140, 10]  
   • x       = [0, 65, 47.5]  
   • y       = [0, 0, 47.5]  
   • z       = [0, 0, 0]  
   • subtraction = [False, False, True]

6. After the block() call, issue finished(allFunctionsCalled=True).

When you are ready for me to write the actual function call payloads, just tell me and I will provide them exactly as needed.
